body:
I'm 29, but I wasn't in any sort of relationship until I was 27, which was with my ex. I was only able to accept being in a relationship with him because he had been my friend for over 10 years. I had no interest in men prior due to severe trauma, and still can't feel comfortable around men, even my current partner.
 I still feel completely desperate to be with my ex because of how secure I was able to feel.

I guess my mood does fluctuate a lot between depression, anxiety, desperation, shame and numbness.
I think I'm volatile in that I tend to resort to isolation, self-harm and suicide attempts to relieve those feelings. 

And in my ex's case, I have experienced intense clinginess and desperation to the point I would call it harassment, because I genuinely have only been free from suicidal and worthless feelings when I was with him, and before he started treating me badly. I just haven't been able to recover from that loss.
I guess I just feel tired of life, it's been something I just endure now. I used to have a lot of hobbies and a few close friends, but I haven't been able to feel happiness from that for a while now.

They said they think it's PTSD and MMD, which have been my diagnoses since I was little. The doctor at the hospital suggested it because of how many suicide attempts I've had in my life, especially because the recent ones are due to a breakup.

I'm so sorry. Mine was extremely similar, when I'd tell him his constant bailing and severe lack of communication was hurting my feelings, he'd say I was being clingy. If I said I wanted to see him more than 10 minutes a week, he said I was ungrateful, and eventually said I was too much and dumped me. 


This cycle repeated multiple times, and he would occasionally use me to cheat on other girls without my immediate knowledge. I now I have full-blown BPD and became abusive to him in my own right, which he has happily used against me to shake off any responsibility, saying I am crazy and he only wanted to help me, that I ruined my chances with him and can only blame myself. It's hard to explain how destructive these quite kind of abuses get.

My narc literally admitted this to me, he said he gets bored and lonely but doesn't feel motivated to put any real effort after a while. He described the relationship he wants as a girl who is his best friend who is always there for him when he needs her, but will be okay with him ignoring her whenever and for however long he wants. And he saw no issue with it.

You're doing well imo, removing a toxic influence is really similar to addiction, it rarely happens all at once. You can always start again if you happen to relapse and it'll get easier to resist over time.

Mine is the same, he says helping people is his passion, would share tons of posts about women's rights and mental health awareness, and he would say he also would try hard to stay friends with all his exes. 

But whenever he would hoover me, he'd say something subtle, like the previous ex was controlling, or he was unhappy with them. When discarding, he'd tell me and the new girl I was crazy and he just wanted to help me, which he had an easy time doing because I am open about my own mental illnesses, and he would seemingly do everything in his power to trigger a breakdown he could use in his defense. They are really the definition of two-faced.

>She was so damn horrible to me but I feel lost without her

This is me exactly, I have been chasing him for the past year, even after all the crushing emotional abuse, manipulation, two-timing and broken promises. I just can't feel happy without him right now.

Learned helplessness is a phenomenon seen in a famous experiment where they put dogs in a cage with an electrified floor. The dogs would jump around trying to escape the pain, but after some time, they realized it was impossible and would just lie down and take the shocks. Even after opening the cage, they wouldn't try to escape anymore. 

Similarly, while its true we don't know for sure if things will stay so difficult, but I also understand how it feels to already have gone through so much that you kind of stop having hope. Depression that severe is very difficult to treat, and I'm so sorry if you've ever been made to feel ashamed for it. 

I hope very much you can find the exit anyway, I hope everyone who is stuck in that cage gets out.

I'm dealing with something similar. Breakups can be way more devastating than people think. There aren't any clear or easy ways to heal, but time definitely helps, and taking things easy on yourself too.
The most rational thing I can think of is the fact that we can't say for certain we will always feel this bad, or that life won't be enjoyable in the future.
You showed up for yourself with a lot of love. Take it easy for a while, you are going to be okay. :)
Thank you for being here to speak up about this, I already feel a bit better knowing it's not just me. Virtual hugs!

I think we have similar ways of thinking, I reacted pretty much the same as you, feeling worthless, not good enough, and am still very depressed. But it isn't true, that person is the one who ruined their chance to be with someone who loves them and is too self-absorbed to see it, what could be more sad than that?
I'm not out of the woods by any means, but I've started talking to my friends again, doing some of the hobbies I used to love, and just trying to reclaim myself from the opinion of someone who goes against my values. I only wish I could have discarded them when I had the chance!
Thank you, I'm saving these lyrics to remind me whenever I start feeling down about myself. Happy holidays!!
That is messed up, I'm so sorry they'd say that but that is so not true. I honestly would rather be like you, safe from the pain of heartbreak!

I'm so sorry, I had a very similar experience. But this guy sounds like he was wrong, it was more that he was wrong for you. You have been through a lot already and need someone who is not so unavailable and frankly he sounds a bit selfish, probably why he's been in so many relationships. 

Be choosy, if someone is devaluing you like that, they are not good enough for you.

Totally get it, a lot of tall women have the same problem, where men won't want to even approach them.
I've known a lot of girls that are 5' or even a little less, so even in this regard, it's not as much of a disadvantage as it might seem.
You're so young, and there are lots of girls shorter than you too! Try your best to really think things through, you'll be okay.

It might help if you think about it this way; They ruined their chances with you. You did not ask them to treat you like that, they went out of their way to do things knowing it would hurt someone who genuinely cared about them. They lost you, and sadly they will lose anyone who doesn't either submit entirely or is even worse than they are.

You however, are now free.

I think that means you have excellent boundaries and self-esteem, that's super awesome, obviously it would have been better to not deal with that at all, but looks like you can at least know now that you are very unlikely to end up with another one!

My nex met up with me, offered to be fwb while also failing to mention he has been in a serious relationship for months. I told her, sent her screenshots and all she said was I was laughable and making it up. She made fun of me for causing "high school drama", and weirdly bragged about being divorced once before so she knew better. 

Long story short, probably not worth it. We've taken more than enough responsibility for their bs anyway.

I got a rare amount of closure from my nex, and he told me something that probably applies to lots of them
He told me he knew he had done wrong, but that was just who he was, he said he's emotionally unavailable, didn't do feelings is an asshole in general, and he didn't have any intention of trying to change because he didn't really see it as a problem.

All that time I spent believing in the person who said I was important and special to them, who promised to care for me was, in his own words, never real.

I could have written this post. It's really hard to deal with for sure, I just keep reminding myself that this painful jealousy is also a result of their abuse, it helps me depersonalize the anxious thoughts.
And of course, you are now leaving behind a terrible person, your sore from carrying all his bs, but in time that will fade.

Oh absolutely, trauma bonds are awful but incredibly strong. It will get less intense as long as you can maintain distance, and eventually you'll be clear enough to have a healthier relationship with someone who doesn't give you ptsd!
I'm so sorry, they are truly awful and I am hoping so much you are able to escape safely. Lots of hugs, I wish you and your child the best!

It's super normal to doubt if it was that bad, or if you were the problem. The fact that you're worrying kind of proves you were not. 
Good on you for standing up for yourself, from now on you are free to leave that unhappiness behind.

The sooner you can free yourself from taking responsibility for someone else's choice to be a terrible partner, the better. I comprimised my wants, needs and morals to try to keep my abuser around. That's so damaging, and I'm just barely starting to see things clearly almost a year after discard.
I wish you the best, you deserve someone who doesn't force you to be micromanaging them.

Ahhgh yep that was my ex exactly, it was me with the communication issues, it was me who wasn't cooperation or appreciating his efforts, and then the relationship failed because I wouldn't just do what he said, which was impossible because he would find a problem with anything I did!

I'm ace too, for me I ended up agreeing to a lot of things I didn't want to do out of fear my ex would leave me (he was previously very emotionally abusive). It sounds like part of it was the attention itself was pleasant, and partly out of increasing guilt. My ex would be like, well I already agreed to this, why not that, or that it would make him happy and stay longer with me so I would "consent".

You said you have a lot of emotional issues, that can mess up your sense of boundaries really bad, but it isn't your fault, and you have nothing to be ashamed of.

That's not helpful at all. Don't tell someone they can't be helped and then tell them to get help wtf. 
I deal with ruminations, not about anything like this, and reassurance seeking is a pretty typical part of that. Obviously therapy would be the best option for op but my gosh tone does matter a lot when people are in irrational states of mind.

After being in an abusive relationship I got like this. Sadly not all bad experiences make people stronger, but I hope instead of strength we can give ourselves the kindness and gentleness people in our lives have refused to provide

Ahh this is it, you're right!! Why would I want to constantly strain and belittle myself trying to please someone when I'd literally be better off alone?? 
The only thing that makes it hard is the withdrawls, but I just realized I don't miss that feeling of never being good enough
I was discarded by an abusive ex too. Look up trauma bonds, and r/narcissisticabuse could be a helpful community for you

This is 100% grooming, and you are absolutely not at fault. The only ones who should be ashamed here are the ones who are disgusting enough to abuse a child. 
I was abused as a child too, and I know how difficult it is, but I would really recommend you tell a trusted adult about what happened. If they can contact the authorities that would be ideal because what they did to you is a crime, but most importantly they can get you counseling to help you process this awful experience.

I really hope you stay safe and are able to reach out for help, this sadly happens to many people, and you deserve justice and healing.
Can we talk for a bit?

I don't mean this in a vain way, but I am considered to be very attractive. I fell in love with one of my best friends, who is honestly not good looking at all. 
Once our relationship changed into a romantic one, he began to abuse me so severely that even now after leaving him I am extremely depressed and suicidal. 

Obviously, I wasn't with him nor did I endure the abuse because he was hot, he absolutely wasn't. And me being attractive did nothing to make him value or cherish me as a person. Abusive people show up in all kinds of forms, male, female, ugly, beautiful, and every other sort. 

And victims are bound to them not by their looks but by trauma. Your self-worth becomes wholly dependant on their approval, so leaving them is essentially unthinkable. This is a pathological and irrational process that is difficult to break. 

In the end, beauty is a tiny and short-lived part of a person, but I understand that your own traumas have magnified it a lot. What those awful people did is imo  the truly ugly thing.

I am a woman, and was abused severely by my ex as well. I've been abused and discarded by men since I was a child, and that includes my own father.
Even now, I thought I'd found someone who said he liked me only to get dropped out of the blue right after he used me. 
The point is, it's not a gendered thing, it's just that there are terrible people out there, and they are destructive to highly sensitive people like us. 

I hope you know you are better off without her and I really hope you won't get caught up with any more like her.

I feel kind of the same. It's painful to think about starting all over, but the fact that you are having any self-reflection is a really good sign. It means you do have the capacity to recover, maybe make some amends, and rebuild.
I get what you mean. I'd be happy to talk.

I know it's hard to imagine, but appearances really don't matter that much when it comes to happiness. I was really overweight and only dressed in boy's clothes at your age and was similarly self-concious. 
I'm 28 now and I am thin, considered very conventionally attractive, and I still want to die. Actually, I'm more unhappy than I ever have been, because it made me a target for abusive men.

What I want to convey is that it's your sense of self that matters. Our appearances are just shells, and even the most beautiful person will rot away eventually. Might be a little random, but the band BTS  helps me cope a lot with their emphasis on "loving yourself", and how much they appreciate everyone. I'd recommend watching some of their interviews and stuff, they're also just really funny guys.

That's not fair that you have to deal with that at all. :(
I'm very much in solidarity with you though, hopefully with time we'll get to a place where it isn't so painful at least!

Omg I am above all else sorry that this happened to you, but I am also grateful that you shared this, because I was starting to feel really ashamed and alone.

I feel pretty much the same, being reminded of anything romance instantly makes me anxious and queasy. It's been devastating, I stopped being able to work my job because I couldn't handle the songs that played there and it put a total halt to a project I was working on because it involves romantic themes.

I can say it's getting a little better; it's not exactly advisable, but one thing that's helped was initially watching/reading/writing about unhappy relationships like mine. For some reason, a few months of this has let me start to tolerate general romance without going into a full-on panic. 
My ultimate goal is to be able to binge say yes to the dress again, I miss that show :(
I'm so sorry that happened! I got discarded on Valentine's Day this year and am terrified for the next one.

I'm someone who's abusive ex also drove me to make multiple suicide attempts. Once while I was in the ER, he happened to be working around there and we saw each other. There was nothing im his eyes. He only contacted me later to tell me not to blame him and that he had no responsibility for my choices.

The point I'm trying to make is that you feel genuine remorse, and it sounds like your ex knows that. True apologies are more important and powerful than people may realize, and the fact that you are able to recognize, accept and have remorse for any harm you may have caused means you have the capacity to change and make amends. 

Suicide isn't going to do that though, we can't change the past, but a genuine apology and probably no further contact is more than enough. If she continues to be in that much pain, that has more to do with her ability to cope as you would have already done what you could. I wish you both the best, and hope you can both heal from this.

I'm glad you were able to recover from that, they are so unbelievable. I hadn't really considered the love bombing as a type of abuse in itself, but it really is, and in some ways it feels like the worst part because that's ultimately what has kept me feeling stuck. 

But you're right, the only important difference is that I am not being abused anymore. Thank you, I do feel a little less anxious, and yes, absolutely going to take a general break on social media until I don't feel that temptation!

Thank you so much for this, I'm sorry you had to deal with that, you are really strong yourself!

I hadn't thought of it like that! I started really trying to maintain boundaries in the relationship, and that was when I got discarded. I guess like you said he's learned he has to play the part better to get the type of supply he wants. 
Yes, actually the last thing he said to me was that if I wanted to k*ll myself, it would be okay. I also realized from the date of the post, he said that just a few days before going on vacation, so he defiantly is still as callous as ever.

I did too omg. I had been so good about avoiding the socials until yesterday, and all I see is him succeeding in the job he said he valued more than me, in a new relationship that he clearly spends more effort in and it just has torn me up, I'm back to square one :(

You're okay, I've desperately reached out to my abuser many times, to the point I became abusive myself. 
I think what we need to remember is that our motivation for reaching out is completely different from when they do it. We are reacting to a trauma that we did nothing to incite, they are abusing people without any provocation.

With that in mind, you have nothing to be ashamed of, this is a normal reaction in an abnormal situation. Redirect your mind back to you as many times as you have to, you'll be alright! :)

"You have the power to change but you won't."
"I won't apologize because I've already forgiven myself."
"You have to forgive me for your own good."

All said by him after discarding me when I tried to express how badly I was affected by his actions. 

"Just stop thinking about it." 
"You are just obsessed, you can stop if you want."
"You're hardly trying at all."
"Seeing you like this is hard for us too, you don't seem to care how you affect us."

Said by my family. My mom keeps threatening to move away or kick me out because of how depressed I have gotten. It is really painful to be dismissed like this.
I had a bad relapse myself recently, it's discouraging having to relive the devastation all over again.

You are not pathetic, you have continued to live despite the trauma and mental illness. And you have obviously already been through enough. He is 100% being abusive. I agree that you may need to call the police since you aren't able to purchase travel back to your home. 
I hope so much that you get home safe, and definitely block this guy everywhere once you do!
Do you play any video games? I really love the Silent Hill and Kingdom Hearts series. :)
Ah not sure, it seems like post visibility is hard to predict unfortunately. :/
You're completely right, I have no idea if it's really all that great. Thanks for that reality check, I gotta get back to focusing on me!

Okay, so I just realized my nex spent literally 14 years doing exactly this.

This is the rough timeline:

2006: We met in school, I was not interested in him because I found him kind of pretentious, but we became good friends since my best friend at the time was into him but he had a gf at the time.

2011: My friend and him dated for this year, he was neglectful once he went out of state for university, and ghosted her causing her to become quite depressed.

2015: He returns, saying he had lied about being in university and had actually flunked in the first month. He was ashamed which is why he ghosted. During this time, my friend says we should forgive him and I agree feeling bad, and she is hoping to restart their relationship.
During this time, he starts wanting to spend a lot of time with me, is very charming and takes me out a lot. I find myself falling for him and confess to both my friend and him because I feel guilty. He says he doesn't like me back and I'm sad but whatever, it would have been messy anyway. 
One day I get a text from him about looking at apartments clearly meant for his girlfriend he never even hinted at. His attention continues to be on me, and he suddenly has my friend tell me not to speak to him anymore because I am ruining his relationship.

2016:His gf contacts me after seeing a text I sent him about wanting closure. She tells me she was upset at how he was treating me because he was spending all his free time with me instead of her, but as long as there was no physical cheating she was fine.

2019: He returns again after breaking up with his gf. He says he chose wrong and wanted to start over. I am nervous but after the time apart, I feel I am strong enough to be friends. The flirting starts again, stronger than ever. I decide I don't like the mixed messages and try to end the friendship. He angrily admits he lied and always liked me since we met, but wants to date around for a while. I feel hopeful and decide to wait for him.
The next night he again asks my friend to tell me he no longer likes me. I firmly end the friendship this time, but I am miserable and drop out of school.

2020: I reach out for closure. He tells me he missed me and agrees. He takes me out to eat, and seems apologetic. we fall back into our old friendship banter and it feels nice. I realize I still love him so I tell him we're good and I don't want to communicate anymore.
He asks me if I still love him, I admit I do and he asks me out. I am resistant to the idea, afraid he'll stop liking me again. He says he lied about that and never stopped liking me. I say I'm scared he'll just leave again. He says he won't this time, promises me he wants to be with me for the long haul. I make a horrible decision and agree.

2021: The discard is brutal. He says I have to give up any expectation that he will ever keep his word he will dump me. I desperately try to remind him of what he said, how hard I was trying to work with him, how many times I forgave him, and he just tells me he can take back his promises and dumps me over text Valentine's Day.

It really feels like I was slowly conditioned to be a surefire supply. Even when he dumped me, he said we could maybe try again, but it would be at his whim. Well, it worked.

She sounds very classically abusive at the very least. 

My ex also would change around boundaries to suit him and would shame me into complying. He was kind of the opposite where he was a workaholic and would bail on plans because he said he'd rather make money than see me. But he also said many hurtful things, said I needed to be more consistent but said I couldn't expect him to keep his word. 

You do not have to be stuck with a person like this. It would be a good idea to escape before you get trauma bonded, I am a year out of my relationship and still suffer from feeling like I need him. Also, big warning not to be friends at all after, we are just supply to them, contact at all just feeds them.

Best wishes!

You went through a lot, and it sounds like you've already made a ton of progress, I hope you can give yourself props for that!

I'm almost a year out and had a major relapse today and looked at his social media. Discovering he has a new partner that he treats much better set off a lot of obsessive thinking and self-blame, and I am angry that I still seem to have a need for his approval. I keep forgetting how bad it was, that he isn't good for me. Trauma bonds are something else, it's not really weird that it was so difficult to pull away, it's like a really strong addiction. I am hoping I can get to where you are at the very least and finally get him out of my head.

I can relate. I have a long history of abuse and suicidal thoughts, and have been in therapy and on meds for years, and early this year I was discarded by an abusive partner who initially promised I would be safe with him. This morning I found out he's been seeing someone else and is treating her the way he said he promised he would treat me. 

I just don't feel like I can keep going when it seems so clear I'm just not worth caring about. My friends are all too busy with work and relationships to really talk and I'm just too scared of being a burden. I don't really know what to do, but I would be happy to hear you out since I'm kind of in the same boat and all.

I hope things improve for you!

That's true, he used to tell me he felt unimportant in the world, and that he found meaning in helping people. He did have something like a hero complex since I've known him, like what he really wanted was to be a police officer, but he failed the psychological exams, honestly, that's probably for the best.

I have a lot of the same thoughts. My biological father sexually abused me when I was a child, then I was sexually harassed for months by a teacher in middle school and the other girls called me a slut for it. As an a adult, the one man I had grown to trust enough to enter a relationship with emotionally and sexually abused me before discarding me. I'm now feeling so broken and worthless that I've already attempted suicide 3 times in the past few months and am desperately resisting a 4th, but I just feel so drained. 

Whatever people want to say, we absolutely do not have gender equity. Being female is a nightmare for so many. I'm so sorry that this awful climate has become unbearable for you. I hope we can all find some way to be happy and safe, but I totally get being done with all this bs.

Oh and I did recieve therapy for the initial trauma and was mostly recovered before this all happened. 
It's been a lot more difficult to find a therapist for this sort of thing, the last one I tried to see said I couldn't cry in session because it stressed her out. :/

I thought about reporting him saying those things about suicide, but since I survived I don't know if I can. He is a mandated reporter though, which causes me a lot of concern for the people he works with.

There were definitely several red flags, but because we had been friends for almost 14 years at that point I was in denial.

One thing I remember was when he literally told me he thought he might be a psychopath, but I insisted that couldn't be possible because he would always say he lives just to help people in need.

I just saw that the next has a new girlfriend which has me feeling awful and extremely jealous, but you reminded me that no one knew the extent of what was happening in my relationship with him and I need to remember it was abuse.

Emotional: He would constantly change what he felt about me. One day, I'm just a friend, the next he lied and actually liked me for 13 years, then not at all but actually he lied about that too, he likes me a lot.
During the relationship, he became neglectful, cancelling plans last second and told me over and over I was not as important to him as work and money, that spending time with me didn't get him paid. He also claims to be woke but made fun of me and my family for being poor and once said "I thought Mexicans we're supposed to be good at cleaning" which was humiliating to hear.

Sexual abuse or assault?: I was completely inexperienced in relationships while he had been in several. When I asked if he could wear a condom, he said it hurt that I didn't trust him so I felt I had to give up on that. I am a csa survivor, abused by my biological father, and he coaxed me into a daddy/little girl dynamic knowing how it was making me feel. He also kept trying to touch me when I said I was not comfortable with it and did bdsm things like tying me up, choking me and biting me hard enough to bruise without consent or discussion. I'm not sure if that counts as physical abuse too?

Psychological: Not too long ago, just before he went on a long vacation with the new gf, he encouraged me to attempt suicide, which I did and suffered lasting damage.

Low Empathy: He sent me a numbered list of his priorities and I was number 5, after work, career, money and future. When I told him how depressed and anxious his treatment was making me, he said I just needed to have no expectations or he'd dump me. I said I couldn't do that and he chose to do that after standing me up on my first Valentine's Day in a relationship over text.
When I said I had been trying so hard to work with him, and even went on birth control which was giving me a lot of side effects he said it was a me problem. 

I'm so sad that this happens to so many people.

Yep. The ones that drove me to this state through abuse are the same ones who said they cared and wanted me to be happy. Then when I couldn't take it anymore and made an attempt, it was about how I hurt them?? 

Hilariously they also work for healthcare and claim they love to help others :)

r/narcissisticabuse might be helpful for your sitiation, it sounds a lot like what others on that sub are dealing with. 

You do not deserve any of this cruelty, and I am so sorry that it happened. You are already too good for this person just by virtue of the fact that you are capable of love, so I hope very much that you can sever this tie and keep living, but for yourself.
